question: Who announced the ₹50,000 mass marriage incentive scheme for minorities in the Karnataka 2025–26 state budget?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Siddaramaiah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister of Karnataka, announced the ₹50,000 mass marriage incentive scheme for minorities in the **Karnataka 2025–26 state budget**.
 
• The scheme is aimed at providing financial assistance to minorities for conducting mass marriages, thereby supporting economically weaker sections of society.
 
• This initiative reflects the government's effort to promote social welfare by addressing financial constraints in marriage ceremonies for minority communities.
 
• Under this scheme, eligible beneficiaries from minority communities will receive a direct incentive of **₹50,000 per couple** during mass marriage events.
 
• The scheme is expected to reduce the economic burden on families and encourage the practice of collective marriage ceremonies, fostering communal harmony.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Siddaramaiah:**

 
 
• Siddaramaiah is a prominent Indian politician and the current **Chief Minister of Karnataka** as of 2025.
 
• He belongs to the **Indian National Congress (INC)** party.
 
• Siddaramaiah has held the position of Chief Minister previously and is known for his focus on social welfare and inclusive development.
 
• He has introduced several schemes targeting marginalized communities, including minorities, farmers, and women.
 
 
 
• **Mass Marriage Incentive Schemes:**
 
 
• Such schemes aim to provide financial assistance for marriage ceremonies, especially for economically weaker sections.
 
• Mass marriages often reduce individual expenses as events and arrangements are organized collectively.
 
• These schemes help address social issues such as financial stress related to dowries or extravagant wedding expenses.
 
• Similar initiatives have been launched by other states, including Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh, to promote communal harmony and reduce wedding costs.
 
 
 
• **Minority Welfare in Karnataka:**
 
 
• Karnataka has been proactive in launching schemes for minority communities, such as education scholarships, housing assistance, and skill development programs.
 
• The state government has set up the **Minority Welfare Department** to address issues and ensure better access to government benefits for minority groups.
 
• Previous schemes include **Shaadi Bhagya**, which provided financial aid to Muslim brides, and **Pre-Matric & Post-Matric Scholarships**.
 
 
 
• **Budgetary Allocation for Social Welfare:**
 
 
• The Karnataka government often allocates a significant portion of its budget to social welfare programs targeting vulnerable groups.
 
• The 2025–26 budget particularly emphasized minority welfare, women empowerment, and rural development.
 
• Mass marriage schemes reflect the government’s commitment to equitable development and addressing financial challenges faced by underprivileged communities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eligibility Criteria:**

 
 
• Beneficiaries must belong to minority communities as defined by the government.
 
• Applicants should fall under the economically weaker sections of society and provide proof of financial status.
 
• The scheme applies to mass marriage ceremonies conducted by registered organizations or religious institutions.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Mass Marriage Schemes:**
 
 
• Encourages social cohesion and reduces individual financial burden.
 
• Promotes the idea of simple, collective wedding ceremonies, reducing extravagance.
 
• Helps foster communal harmony among different communities participating in mass marriage events.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Mass marriage schemes have been implemented across India to address issues like dowry, financial strain, and social inequality.
 
• Such schemes are rooted in the idea of promoting equality and ensuring that marriage does not become a financial burden on families.
